text:
anya: Heads-up — perf regression seen in long-context mix on the replay harness after the new kernel selector landed. p95 prefill latency is ~28% higher vs baseline.

mike: Ugh. Is this prefill-dominant only, or also steady-state decoding?

anya: Mostly prefill-heavy cases (seqlen > 8k), context-mix that has ~30% prefill weight. Decoding tails look fine.

kai: Any KV cache hit-rate change? That can blow up prefill if lookups missed.

anya: KV hit-rate stable on the harness (98%), but the kernel selector is choosing the tiled transformer kernel for the big sequences which has higher setup cost in our implementation.

reena: Can you paste the replay command you used?

anya: Sure —
```
./replay_harness --profile --seed 42 --mix configs/longtail_context_mix.json \ 
  --model rdm-13b-qlora --kv-warm=true --replay-window 1000
```

mike: Did you run apples-to-apples vs the previous binary? same build flags, same quant path?

anya: Yes, we've reproduced with both binaries on the same image. Only changed the runtime commit (kernel selector 2.1). Baseline commit: 2059856, Head: 2060123.

perf-ci: Automated run summary: baseline p95_prefill=42ms, head p95_prefill=54ms, p50_prefill unchanged ~12ms, overall tokens/s decreased ~9% for that mix. Flame graphs attached to the CI artifact: /artifacts/2060323456/flame_prefill.svg

sam: Interesting p50 unchanged but p95 up — points to tail variance maybe due to kernel switch heating caches or scheduling. Do we have per-kernel timings?

anya: Yes, quick aggregate: tiled_kernel prefill avg=60ms, smallseq_kernel prefill avg=38ms on same seq lengths where smallseq would have been picked earlier. Selector picked tiled_kernel for >2k seqs now.

kai: Could be our kernel cost model mis-estimating for prefill because prefill has larger KV flush / memory traffic. The selector cost model assumes steady-state decode cost not the one-time prefill overhead.

reena: So methodology note — apples-to-apples must include both the exact sequence-length distribution and whether requests are prefill-first or incremental. We should add an explicit prefill-heavy synthetic scenario to the standard suite.

anya: Agreed. Proposed immediate mitigation: add selector override for prefill flag so we prefer smallseq_kernel for prefill paths until we fix model. Patch idea: `--prefill-force-kernel=smallseq` or fallback after a latency threshold.

mike: Do we have telemetry to toggle that remotely? Ops could flip a config for affected customers.

infra-bot: Canary config rollout is available via /ops/runtime/selector_flags. Can enable `prefill_force_smallseq=true` for dedicated pools.

sam: For the benchmark protocol, let's standardize: 1) run replay vs synthetic longtail with identical seed and timing, 2) ensure KV warm/cold cases are tested, 3) collect per-kernel microbench and nvprof traces for hot paths, 4) compare token throughput and p95 prefills.

anya: I'll run a head-to-head with: baseline selector, head selector, head selector + prefill override. Will attach profiler traces and a small reproducer that hits a few 8k-12k sequences.

reena: Also add a short doc snippet about how to do apples-to-apples: describe sequence length bucketing, request interarrival distribution (Poisson vs constant), and cache-warm policy. Put it under docs/benchmarks/longmix-guidelines.md.

kai: For longer-term: update cost model to include prefill startup cost: measure KV memory store/restore time and kernel init cost, then penalize tiled path for prefill weight.

mike: Action items: anya run the three runs and upload traces (owner: anya, due EOD), kai to draft selector cost model change (owner: kai, due Wed), reena to add benchmark doc (owner: reena, due Fri), sam to coordinate config canary (owner: sam).

anya: Starting runs now. Will post links when done. cc @perf-ci for automated verification. :thumbsup:

perf-ci: Noted — will kick off regression job once traces are uploaded.

anya: Quick note — one repro difference we found: synthetic generators that pad to max_seq cause selector to always prefer tiled_kernel; make sure mix generator preserves true seq length distribution rather than padding.

mike: Good catch. That could silently bias apples-to-apples tests.

anya: Yup. Ok running now.
